::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## What this lesson is for

This is where the data starts answering real questions: *What is the total catch at each site? Which
gear brings in the most? How many trips were recorded last month?*

All of these are **"add it up by group"** questions. This lesson shows you how, with two commands.
Press **Run** on each box. Remember: **you cannot break anything.**
:::

Run the box below once to switch on **dplyr** (as in the last lesson) and load the small example table.

```{webr}
#| autorun: true
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

example <- data.frame(
  trip_id      = c("trip_1", "trip_1", "trip_1", "trip_2", "trip_2"),
  landing_date = c("2024-01-05", "2024-01-05", "2024-01-05", "2024-01-06", "2024-01-06"),
  site         = c("Shimoni", "Shimoni", "Shimoni", "Vanga", "Vanga"),
  gear         = c("hand line", "hand line", "hand line", "gillnet", "gillnet"),
  fish         = c("Tilapia", "Snapper", "Octopus", "Tilapia", "Snapper"),
  catch_kg     = c(12, 5, 3, 8, 6)
)
example
```

## One number for your whole table

**`summarise()`** turns a whole column into a single answer. To add up all the weights, you give the
answer a name (`total_kg`) and tell R to `sum` the `catch_kg` column. Press **Run**:

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
example |>
  summarise(total_kg = sum(catch_kg))
```

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
**What you should see:** one row with **`total_kg = 34`** — the weight of all five catches added
together (12 + 5 + 3 + 8 + 6). The part `total_kg =` is just the **name** you chose for the answer.
:::

You can ask for more than one answer at a time. **`n()`** counts the rows. Press **Run**:

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
example |>
  summarise(total_kg = sum(catch_kg), number_of_catches = n())
```

## A number for each group

A single total for everything is rarely what you want. Usually you want **one total per site**, or per
gear, or per month. That is what **`group_by()`** is for: you tell R which column to group on, and then
`summarise()` gives you **one answer for each group**.

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
example |>
  group_by(site) |>
  summarise(total_kg = sum(catch_kg))
```

Read it as: *take the example, **group by** site, **then** add up the weight in each group.* Here is what
that does to the rows:

```{=html}
<style>
tr.s1 td { background:#dbe9f6 !important; }   /* Shimoni — blue */
tr.s2 td { background:#fdebd0 !important; }   /* Vanga — amber */
.agg-wrap { display:flex; gap:18px; align-items:center; flex-wrap:wrap; margin:.6rem 0; }
.agg-arrow { font-size:1.6rem; color:#666; }
.agg-wrap table { width:auto; font-size:.9rem; }
</style>
<div class="agg-wrap">
<table class="table">
  <thead><tr><th>site</th><th>catch_kg</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr class="s1"><td>Shimoni</td><td>12</td></tr>
    <tr class="s1"><td>Shimoni</td><td>5</td></tr>
    <tr class="s1"><td>Shimoni</td><td>3</td></tr>
    <tr class="s2"><td>Vanga</td><td>8</td></tr>
    <tr class="s2"><td>Vanga</td><td>6</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
<div class="agg-arrow">&#8594;</div>
<table class="table">
  <thead><tr><th>site</th><th>total_kg</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr class="s1"><td>Shimoni</td><td>20</td></tr>
    <tr class="s2"><td>Vanga</td><td>14</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
</div>
```
*Each site's rows collapse into one total: Shimoni's three rows (12 + 5 + 3) become **20**; Vanga's two
(8 + 6) become **14**.*

## More than one summary, on any column

You can group by **any** column, and ask for several summaries at once. **`mean()`** gives the average.
This groups by the kind of fish and shows the total, the average, and the count for each:

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
example |>
  group_by(fish) |>
  summarise(
    total_kg   = sum(catch_kg),
    average_kg = mean(catch_kg),
    number     = n()
  )
```

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
**What you should see:** one row per kind of fish — Tilapia, Snapper, Octopus — each with its total
weight, its average weight, and how many catches there were.
:::

## Now your own data

Let's total the catch **per landing site** in your real data. Real records sometimes have a **missing**
weight; `na.rm = TRUE` tells R to skip those so you still get an answer. Press **Run**:

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
landings |>
  group_by(gaul_2_name) |>
  summarise(total_kg = sum(catch_kg, na.rm = TRUE))
```

## Put it all together

This is the real reward. Using everything from the last two lessons, you can answer a proper question
like *"in my district, how much does each gear bring in?"* — **filter** to your site, **group by** gear,
then **add up**. Press **Run**, then change `"Vanga"` to one of your own sites:

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
landings |>
  filter(gaul_2_name == "Vanga") |>
  group_by(gear) |>
  summarise(
    total_kg = sum(catch_kg, na.rm = TRUE),
    number   = n()
  )
```

## What you have learned

- **`summarise(name = sum(column))`** — add a column up into one answer (also `mean()` for the average,
  `n()` for a count).
- **`group_by(column)`** before `summarise()` — get **one answer per group** instead of one overall.
- **`na.rm = TRUE`** — skip missing values so you still get a result.

Put together with `filter` and `select` from the last lesson, you can now answer most everyday questions
about your data: totals and averages, for any group, in any part of your records. That is the whole
toolkit — well done.
